narrative:
On September 1, 2026, the Karnataka High Court addressed a heavy caseload of 2,520 scheduled cases across 41 judges, ultimately hearing 1,038 matters. This resulted in an overall hearing rate of 41.2%. Compared to the previous day of August 31, 2026, when the court achieved a 44.6% hearing rate out of 2,153 scheduled cases, the court experienced a minor drop in clearance efficiency despite managing a larger case volume. 

Individual judge performance varied significantly. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 maintained a strong pace, hearing 103 of 202 scheduled cases (51.0%). Justice M. Nagaprasanna in Hall 14 also delivered high output, resolving 140 cases across two sessions out of 254 scheduled. On the other hand, the court's overall performance was weighed down by Hall 2A under T.M. Nadaf, where none of the 240 scheduled cases were heard. Strong clearance rates were observed under Justice Venkatesh Naik T, who heard 46 of 64 cases (71.9%), and Justice S Rachaiah, who heard 36 of 51 cases (70.6%).

Stage-wise conversion metrics show that "Orders" remained the most active category, converting 377 of 746 scheduled cases (50.5%), a decrease from yesterday’s 55.3% conversion rate. "Admission" stages completed 42.8% of 423 cases. However, "Final Hearings" struggled to progress, converting only 19.6% of 598 scheduled cases, down from yesterday's 27.1%.

Regarding case type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the largest share of the docket with 1,113 scheduled cases, of which 432 were heard (38.8%), down from the 42.4% recorded on August 31. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) registered a 37.7% conversion rate (156 of 414), while Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) performed relatively well, with 147 of 287 cases heard (51.2%).
